nexomod.settings.title: Nexo Settings
nexomod.settings.appearance.title: Appearance
nexomod.settings.positionObscuring.title: Position Obscuring
nexomod.settings.obscure.preset.tooltip: None turns all position obscuring off, Full turns everything on, Custom uses the toggles below.
nexomod.settings.obscure.coords.tooltip: Shifts the X/Z coordinates on the F3 screen by a random 3k–700k blocks, re-rolled every time you join a world or server.
nexomod.settings.obscure.blockRotation.t: Random block textures (grass, stone, sand...) normally rotate based on your real position, which screenshots can be matched against. This re-seeds them from the fake coordinates so the pattern agrees with what F3 shows.
nexomod.settings.obscure.bedrockFloor.to: The bedrock pattern at the bottom of the world is generated from the world seed, so a screenshot of it can reveal your coordinates. This renders everything at Y -60 and below as solid bedrock (visual only — mining and collision are unaffected).
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.title: Bedrock Hole Finder
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.enabled.to: Scans loaded chunks for gaps sealed inside the bedrock layers — the Overworld floor, the Nether floor, and the Nether roof — and outlines every enclosed block through the terrain. No world seed needed, so it also finds openings other players broke.
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.radius.too: How far out to scan. Chunks are only scanned once they have loaded, so a range beyond your render distance fills in as you travel.
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.minSize.to: Ignore sealed pockets smaller than this. World generation leaves single blocks of deepslate walled into the bedrock all over the place; raising this to 2 or 3 hides them and leaves the openings worth walking to.
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.maxSize.to: How big a sealed pocket can be and still count as a hole. The finder walks through everything that isn't bedrock; anything bigger than this is ordinary rock connected to the rest of the world, not a gap in the layer.
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.labels.too: Show the kind of hole and its distance in the world, above the nearest ones.
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.chat.toolt: Print the coordinates of newly found holes within 128 blocks to chat — the only notification that leaves the coordinates readable afterwards.
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.toast.tool: Pop a notification in the top-right corner instead of touching chat. It fades after a few seconds, taking the coordinates with it.
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.coords.too: Whether chat and toast notifications name the coordinates of a find. Turn this off while streaming — you still get the hole's size and how far away it is, and the outline in the world still shows you where. Coordinates are also withheld automatically whenever Position Obscuring is hiding your F3 coordinates.
nexomod.settings.bedrockHoles.sound.tool: Play a chime when a hole is found, so you notice one while flying with your eyes on the terrain. At most one per tick, however many are found at once.
nexomod.bedrockHoles.label: %s — %sm
nexomod.settings.chat.title: Chat
nexomod.settings.chat.history.tooltip: Write every chat line you see into a local database so you can search it later. The file never leaves this machine. Off by default — everything else in these settings changes how your own client looks, this one writes down what other people said.
nexomod.settings.chat.filter.tooltip: Apply your pattern list to incoming chat: hide the matches you don't want to see, highlight the ones you do. Harmless with no patterns, so it's on by default.
nexomod.chat.unavailable: Nexo's native core isn't available on this platform — chat history and filtering are inactive.
nexomod.chat.search.title: Chat History
nexomod.chat.search.range.tooltip: Only show messages seen within this window. Applied to the results after the search runs, so a narrow window can return fewer rows than the result limit.
nexomod.chat.search.unavailable: Nexo's native core isn't available on this platform, so there is no chat history to search.
nexomod.chat.filters.title: Chat Filter Patterns
nexomod.chat.filters.help: Regular expressions, matched against each incoming line.
nexomod.chat.filters.action.tooltip: Click to switch between hiding a matching message and highlighting it.
nexomod.servers.title: Quick Servers
nexomod.servers.join.tooltip: Leave the current world and connect to this server.
nexomod.settings.tactical.title: Tactical Features
nexomod.settings.tactical.enabled.toolti: Show where a sound came from, as a marker on a ring around the crosshair. Vanilla subtitles already tell you left or right; this gives the full bearing and fades the marker with distance.
nexomod.settings.tactical.range.tooltip: Sounds further away than this are ignored entirely.
nexomod.settings.tactical.labels.tooltip: Put the subtitle text next to each marker, the way vanilla subtitles do. Sounds with no subtitle stay unlabelled.
nexomod.settings.armorHud.enabled.toolti: Show your armor pieces and their remaining durability down the right edge of the screen.
nexomod.settings.armorHud.warn.tooltip: Remaining durability at or below which a piece's percentage turns red.
nexomod.settings.environment.time.toolti: Fix what time your client thinks it is. Visual only — the server keeps its own clock, so mobs, crops, phantoms and sleeping are all unaffected. The day count keeps advancing, so the moon phase still changes.
nexomod.settings.environment.weather.too: Fix what weather your client draws. Visual only — the server decides the real weather, so this cannot stop a storm, change a spawn, or charge a creeper.
nexomod.settings.chunkHistory.enabled.to: Record the terrain outline of every chunk the server sends you, in a local database.
nexomod.settings.chunkHistory.unavailabl: Chunk history needs the full native core (not built for this platform)
nexomod.settings.chunkHistory.query.tool: Runs a background query over the stored chunks around you and reports how many it found.
nexomod.settings.macroTriggers.enabled.t: Let rules run a macro when something changes — a tool about to break, low health. Each rule fires once when its condition becomes true and then has to reset. Nothing here clicks, swings, or uses an item for you.
nexomod.macroTriggers.title: Trigger Rules
nexomod.macroTriggers.help: A rule fires once when its condition becomes true, then waits for it to go false again.
nexomod.macroTriggers.condition.tooltip: What has to happen for this rule to fire.
nexomod.macroTriggers.macro.tooltip: Which macro's commands to send. Pick from the macros you've defined under Macros.
nexomod.macroTriggers.swap.tooltip: Also select the hotbar slot holding the healthiest copy of the same item. Only changes which slot is selected — the same thing the scroll wheel does — and never moves anything between slots.

nexomod.coords.xaeroWarning: Nexo can't hide coordinates in Xaero's Minimap — it is showing your real position

nexomod.macros.title: Nexo Macros
nexomod.macros.deleteConfirm: Remove the macro "%s"? This can't be undone.
nexomod.macros.name: Name
nexomod.macros.commandsLabel: Commands — sent in order. Start with / for a command, otherwise it's sent as chat. Placeholders: %myname%, %pos%, %x%, %y%, %z%, %clipboard%
nexomod.macros.field.posInt: Must be a positive whole number
